subject: Post-demo: Vireo data handling options and proposed next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Laura Kim <laura.kim@vireohealth.com>, Vireo Security <security@vireohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T21:05:00Z
Subject: Post-demo: Vireo data handling options and proposed next steps

Laura / Vireo Security — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we draft formal language.

Key takeaways from demo:
- Primary concern: minimizing exposure of PHI/PII in transcription & debug logs; must avoid transcript persistence beyond troubleshooting windows.
- Residency: production inference must remain in US-only GCP region for now.
- Audit/evidence: Vireo needs SOC 2 snapshot and sample retention controls for procurement approval.

Options discussed (high level):
1) 0-retention mode for end-user transcripts: transcripts are returned to the customer and not persisted in Redwood KV/cache or disk. Short-lived in-memory KV only; no write-to-disk.
2) Shortened rolling logs: 7-day rolling logs with redaction hooks for obvious PII fields (SSN, full DOB).
3) Route-level retention: ops can configure per-route retention (e.g., clinical summary route = 0-retention; analytics route = 30-day).
4) Encryption + customer-managed keys (optional): for Dedicated/Private customers.

Open asks from Vireo we captured:
- A formal 0-retention option statement and operational constraints (what we can and cannot guarantee).
- Evidence for SOC 2 controls and a short list of artifacts we can provide.
- Any feasibility notes on keeping KV-cache ephemeral but still supporting latency SLOs.

Proposed next steps (suggested timeline):
- I will circulate a concise options paper with three discrete proposals (0-retention, 7-day redacted, per-route schedule) by end of day tomorrow. (Attachment: redwood-data-retention-options.pdf)
- Vireo sec team to confirm whether the procurement bar is satisfied by SOC 2 snapshot + attestation (please advise).
- If 0-retention is a requirement, we propose a short tech feasibility spike (2 weeks) and an ops runbook for onboarding.

If agreeable, I’ll convert the options into a mutual action plan and include a sample contractual clause for the retention carveout so your legal/ procurement can triage.

Attachments referenced: redwood-data-retention-options.pdf (options matrix), mutual-action-plan-DN-4781.xlsx (timeline/action owners), SOC2 snapshot (soc2-snapshot-2026-08.pdf).

Thanks — Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132
From: Laura Kim <laura.kim@vireohealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Vireo Security <security@vireohealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T22:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Vireo data handling options and proposed next steps

Jonas — thanks for the clear recap. Helpful. A few notes from our side: we appreciate the options you outlined.

A couple of clarifying questions before we go to procurement: 
- For 0-retention mode, can you confirm whether any aggregated telemetry (latency buckets, error codes) is stored beyond the in-memory window? We need assurance site-wide telemetry does not carry PII.
- For the 7-day redacted logs, does Redwood perform automated PII redaction or is that a best-effort that requires our pre-defined regex patterns?
- Residency: US-only is a must for production. Staging in other regions is acceptable with flagging.

Procurement ask: If you can provide SOC 2 snapshot and a short note describing the operational controls that back the 0-retention claim, we can submit to procurement next week.

We’re leaning toward trying a pilot with the route-level retention approach (clinical summaries = 0-retention; triage chat = 7-day redacted) but need to validate that 0-retention doesn’t break model-level caching/latency.

Can you put the options paper and a one-page operational note on the impact to latency (worst-case numbers) in HubSpot / Drive so our sec/procurement folks can consume?

— Laura
Laura Kim
Head of Product, Vireo Health
laura.kim@vireohealth.com | +1 (646) 555-0199
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-11T09:00:00Z
Subject: FW: Post-demo: Vireo data handling options and proposed next steps (internal coordination)

Team — forwarding Laura's reply. High level ask from Vireo: they want a formal 0-retention statement + SOC 2 evidence and a latency impact estimate for per-route 0-retention vs normal ops. Proposed approach:

1) Marissa — can you confirm product constraints: what parts of the runtime rely on persisted KV/cache vs in-memory ephemeral KV? Can we support true in-memory-only transcript handling without dropping latency SLAs? If not, detail mitigations.
2) Neha — can you draft the one-page operational note for procurement that explains the controls, redaction options (automated vs pattern-based), and the evidence we can share (SOC 2 snapshot + sample config screenshots).
3) Aditya — legal: we will likely need a short retention carveout clause for the contract and a mutual action plan that lists the pilot acceptance criteria. Can you propose language we can share with Vireo legal?

I'll assemble the options paper and preliminary MAP draft and drop into the shared Drive folder (link below) by EOD. If we can get your inputs by EOD tomorrow, I’ll push the formal package to the prospect.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cVireo-Data-Retention
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DN-4781

Thanks — Jonas
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Laura Kim <laura.kim@vireohealth.com>, Vireo Security <security@vireohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-11T15:45:00Z
Subject: Formal proposal: Vireo retention options + pilot MAP (DN-4781)

Laura / Vireo Sec — attaching the materials we discussed. Summary in-line and ask at the bottom.

What we are proposing (concise):
- Option A — 0-retention profile (pilot): transcripts never written to disk; ephemeral KV held in memory for up to 30s to preserve generation performance; no persisted debug logs for that route. Intended for clinical-summary route only.
- Option B — 7-day redacted logs: automated PII redaction applies (names, email, SSN patterns); customers can provide additional regex for edge cases. Logs are rotated and deleted at day-7.
- Option C — per-route retention configuration: combine A/B across routes; administrative controls in Console to pin retention per model/route.

Operational impacts / controls:
- Latency: Option A (ephemeral KV) shows median +5ms, p99 +22ms in our lab tests; Option B identical to baseline for inference but additional CPU for redaction at log-time (negligible for <300 req/s). Full numbers in the attached PDF.
- Evidence: attaching our SOC 2 snapshot and a short ops note describing log handling and deletion workflows.
- Residency: confirmed — production will be provisioned in US-only region for the pilot.

Attachments (sent): redwood-data-retention-options.pdf (options + latency appendix); mutual-action-plan-DN-4781.xlsx (owners/timeline/acceptance criteria); soc2-snapshot-2026-08.pdf

Requested asks from Vireo to move to pilot:
1) Vireo to approve pilot acceptance criteria (see MAP tab: data flows, test prompt set, success criteria for false positives/negatives in redaction).
2) Vireo sec to confirm whether SOC 2 snapshot + our ops note satisfy procurement or whether you require an on-site review.
3) Signature on MAP by both teams to start the 2-week feasibility spike.

If you'd like, we can schedule a short 30-minute follow-up tomorrow to walk the MAP and the latency appendix with your sec/engineering.

Best — Jonas
